english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=2x^{2}-2x$, and let $R=\left\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}:|x|+|y|\le 1,\ |y|\ge\left|f(|x|)\right|\right\}$. Then the area of $R$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=2x^{2}-2x$ द्वारा परिभाषित है, तथा $R=\left\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}:|x|+|y|\le 1,\ |y|\ge\left|f(|x|)\right|\right\}$ है। तब $R$ का क्षेत्रफल ______ है।
solution: Only $|x|,|y|$ appear, so area $=4\times$ first-quadrant part. For $0\le x\le 1$: $|f(x)|=2x-2x^{2}$ (a hump with top $\frac12$ at $x=\frac12$).
Need $2x-2x^{2}\le y\le 1-x$: possible iff $2x^{2}-3x+1\ge 0\Leftrightarrow(2x-1)(x-1)\ge 0\Leftrightarrow x\le\frac12$ (for $\frac12<x<1$ the hump is above the square's side).
solution_full: $R$ is described through $|x|$ and $|y|$ only, so it is symmetric about both axes and its area is four times the area of its part in the first quadrant.

Graph of $y=|f(|x|)|$: for $x\ge0$, $f(x)=2x(x-1)\le 0$ on $[0,1]$, so $|f(|x|)|=2x-2x^{2}$ there, a hump from $(0,0)$ to $(1,0)$ with greatest value $\dfrac12$ at $x=\dfrac12$; reflecting gives a second hump on $[-1,0]$.

First quadrant: $y\ge 2x-2x^{2}$ and $x+y\le 1$. A vertical segment exists iff $2x-2x^{2}\le 1-x$, i.e. $2x^{2}-3x+1\ge 0$, $(2x-1)(x-1)\ge 0$. For $0\le x\le 1$ this holds exactly when $x\le\dfrac12$ (or $x=1$, a single point).
So the hump touches the side $x+y=1$ at $\left(\dfrac12,\dfrac12\right)$ and for $\dfrac12<x<1$ lies above it; there is no part of $R$ there.
originality_note: New: the square |x| + |y| <= 1 with the double hump |y| < |f(|x|)| removed, where the humps reach the square's sides at (+-1/2, +-1/2) and cover the corners beyond (way 5). Closest known: area inside |x| + |y| <= 1 outside a parabola. Different because: the graph must be built through f(|x|) and the modulus, and the part 1/2 < |x| < 1 drops out entirely.

concept_use.Area of regions bounded by modulus curve: The square |x| + |y| <= 1 gives the upper bound y = 1 - x in the first quadrant.
concept_use.Graphs of |f(x)|, f(|x|), |f(|x|)| and m: The boundary |y| = |f(|x|)| is drawn by reflecting f on [0,1] in the y-axis and taking the modulus: humps 2|x| - 2x^2.

stem_review: Read as a student: every function and curve introduced with its domain, every condition stated, one reading, answer unique and equal to the plan; Hindi mirrors the English maths. Region given as a set; the value 5/6 = 0.8333 rounds unambiguously to 0.83. No change.
key_step: Draw |f(|x|)| and see that it crosses the square's side at x = 1/2, so the part with |x| > 1/2 is empty.
justification: Graph transformation, symmetry and a crossing that removes part of the range; a slip (integrating to x = 1) gives a wrong answer; numerical. L3 like 2026-P2-Q18.
